question.text: Under SEBI regulations, when two mutual fund schemes of the same AMC are being merged or consolidated, unitholders must be:

answer.text: Given adequate notice of the merger and provided an option to exit at NAV without exit load before the merger takes effect
Automatically transferred to the surviving scheme without any notice or exit option
Required to submit fresh KYC documents and a new application form for the surviving scheme
Given the option to exit only if SEBI specifically orders it in each individual case

explanation.text: The Logic: A scheme merger or consolidation is treated, from the unitholders' standpoint, much like a change in fundamental attributes — the basic scheme they invested in is being altered. The protective framework therefore requires AMCs to give unitholders adequate written notice and a window to exit at the applicable NAV without exit load before the merger takes effect, so that an investor who does not want to continue in the surviving scheme can redeem without penalty. The Trap: Automatic transfer without notice would defeat the merger procedures designed to protect unitholders' interests. Fresh KYC is not required when units are merely shifted within the same AMC structure. The exit window is a built-in regulatory protection, not a relief that has to be obtained case by case from SEBI. Note: The Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook states on the cited pages that merger procedures must protect unitholders' interests and discusses changes in fundamental attributes, but does not, on those pages, spell out the exact "adequate notice + exit at NAV without exit load" rule for mergers and consolidations. That framing comes from the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations 1996 and related SEBI circulars rather than from the workbook pages checked.
